lead.hed: U.S. and Indian armies closed three weeks of training in India
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Sunday from Auli: U.S. and Indian Army forces closed Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 in a ceremony Sept. 27, ending three weeks of bilateral training at Auli and Mahajan Field Firing Range. The 22nd iteration paired the 11th Airborne Division's 1st Mobile Brigade Combat Team with the Indian Army for jungle training, combined air assault, and live fire that included HIMARS. Col. Ben Jackman said the point was soldiers who know each other's equipment if they are ever called to fight together. Official still from the closing formation.
lead.image_credit: 2nd Lt. Hannah Allebaugh · DVIDS 9969156 · Public domain · U.S. and Indian Army soldiers in formation at the Yudh Abhyas 2026 closing ceremony, Auli, India, Sept. 27, 2026.

political.hed: British police arrested five men near a U.S. bomber base in England
political.insight: Defense News, Sunday afternoon, citing Reuters: British police arrested five men near RAF Fairford after a tip that three vans were heading toward the airfield, which hosts U.S. Air Force personnel and has been used to strike Iran. President Trump said the suspects had been looking to do big damage and had been under investigation by British and U.S. authorities. Counter Terrorism Policing said the five remain in custody on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, and that police believe the incident is contained. A source familiar with the investigation told Reuters an Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely. Arrest report, not a completed prosecution.

political.hed: A new indictment names Mexican state officials in a cartel case
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: the commentary says the administration shifted from targeting cartel workers to a Justice Department indictment that names ten past and present officials of Mexico's ruling party in Sinaloa, including Governor Rubén Rocha Moya. All ten have denied wrongdoing. Commentary on an indictment, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

political.hed: Treating a child as the opposite sex is not the legal definition of abuse, a report argues
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: institutions built to protect children are under scrutiny after parents lost custody for refusing to treat a gender-confused child as the opposite sex. The report says those cases rest on an ideological premise, not the legal definition of abuse. Report, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

tech.hed: The Navy is weighing foreign designs for the next small warship
tech.insight: USNI News, Sunday: both U.S. and foreign designs for the next small-surface combatant are under consideration after the cancellation of the Constellation-class guided-missile frigate, the new head of the Navy's shipbuilding enterprise said this week. A foreign design study is running in parallel with HII's FF(X) patrol frigate work. Design study, not a contract award.

tech.hed: An essay says progressive stories took public blows at the end of summer
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: the essay says it was a rough end of summer for mainstream progressive narratives, and points to congressional hearings on Anthony Fauci's coronavirus statements and to former NBA players challenging the gender-identity claim. Essay, not a statute.

culture.hed: WORLD reports on China's religious crackdowns
culture.insight: WORLD News Group, Thursday: the piece is filed under the headline Exposing China's religious crackdowns. WORLD's full text sits behind the site's reader wall; the headline and date are from the authorized feed. Report on persecution, not a new U.S. statute.

culture.hed: A third essay takes up the Christian Sabbath
culture.insight: TruthScript, Wednesday, reprinting a Presbyterian Polity piece with the author's permission: the third installment continues a biblical and theological case for the Christian Sabbath begun in the first two articles. Theology essay, not a news event.
